trickyParts: Live claims are 'pending' until the host settles them; a sweep leaves a hole at a pending identity so a later live failure is retried, and a live frame the renderer suppressed must not stay pending (pi-envoy never claims skipped frames; claude-envoy releases them).

Whether a failed live frame is retried by a sweep comes from the engine (liveFailed): only a non-role frame on a subject the latest successful replay answered and that has a cursor; anything else (old listener 404, REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE, team topic, role forward, uncursored subject) gets the notice at once, so nothing is silently dropped.
Strict stream order across subjects in one sweep: the engine buffers what a page read and shows only below the lowest cut point of cut-short subjects; persisted cursors are capped there.
Heartbeat sweeps that only move cursors to the watermark write no state (at most hourly), so the Oh My Pi transcript does not grow per heartbeat.
A local go run rewrites packages/envoy/infra/go.work.sum with this pod's Go; the head keeps main's copy.
deviations: Replayed targeted frames are shown as cards; the plan's stated reason ('Dispatch already recorded that attempt as not delivered') is wrong — the listener answers 200 once it publishes, so Dispatch records the send. Code comments and docs give only the stale-input reason.
Failure counts are kept in memory, so after a restart a failing frame gets three more tries before its notice; a shown notice is in the ledger and is never repeated.

The one-time 404/REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE/401/403 notice is raised at the first failed replay call (not only at start) and can be raised again after a later success; pi-envoy shows it as a UI warning, claude-envoy on stderr.
